newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-WALES RECALL JONATHAN DAVIES AT FLY-HALF.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-WALES RECALL JONATHAN DAVIES AT FLY-HALF.

text.p: Jonathan Davies has been recalled to the Wales' side for Sunday's test against Australia eight years after winning his last cap.
The 34-year-old fly-half switched to rugby league in 1989 but returned to rugby union with Cardiff after the game became professional last year.
He takes over from Welsh record points scorer Neil Jenkins.
"This is a very real surprise, all I can hope for now is that everything goes well on the day," Davies said.

"I feel disappointed for Neil, we are great friends, but sport can be an up and down business. He has taken a lot of knocks but he is a tremendous player, the best goalkicker in the world, and I am sure he will be back.
"I am there to do a job on Sunday and it won't be for the the want of trying. Hopefully, the crowd will get right behind us."
Coach Kevin Bowring said the selectors had taken into account the formidable physical challenge presented by Australia.
"As far as the back division is concerned Jonathan's recall is a direct result of his outstanding form," Bowring said.
"We have long term goals as well as short term objectives and Jonathan's selection is part of the latter."

Prop David Young, another former league player, returns after a seven-year break in place of Neath captain John Davies, while former skipper Ieuan Evans replaces Simon Hill on the wing. Evans was injured for the match against Italy on October 5, won 31-22 by Wales.

Wales - Wayne Proctor; Ieuan Evans, Gareth Thomas, Scott Gibbs, Dafydd James; Jonathan Davies, Rob Howley; Steve Williams, Kingsley Jones, Hemi Taylor, Gareth Llewellyn, Derwyn Jones, David Young, Jonathan Humphreys (captain), Christian Loader.
